Organizations should establish clear reporting procedures to ensure fraud incidents are reported promptly, appropriate stakeholders are informed, and regulatory obligations are met. Timely reporting also supports industry collaboration and fraud trend analysis.

topics.title: 14. Maintaining an Account After Fraud
topics.summary: Organizations do not always close an account after fraud. Depending on the circumstances, they may retain the customer relationship while applying enhanced monitoring and additional fraud controls. The decision depends on regulatory requirements, contractual obligations, customer behaviour, and the organization's risk appetite.
focus: Account maintenance is based on risk, not automatically on fraud occurrence.

topics.title: 15. Customer Exit After a Fraud Investigation
topics.summary: If fraud is confirmed and the customer is responsible, organizations may terminate the relationship. The customer exit process depends on the fraud typology, severity, internal policies, and regulatory requirements. First-party fraud generally results in more severe action than third-party fraud.

topics.title: 16. Case Example – The Money Mule Mastermind
topics.summary: A bank investigated long-standing customer John, who used stolen employee login credentials to process unauthorized vendor payments totaling over US$950,000 through money mule accounts. After gathering sufficient evidence, the bank immediately froze and closed John's account, permanently blacklisted him, strengthened security controls for affected employees, documented the investigation, and reported the case to regulators and law enforcement.

topics.title: Fraud Feedback Loop
topics.summary: The fraud feedback loop transforms investigation findings into long-term improvements. Fraud analytics, investigations, and risk management collaborate to identify root causes, recommend control enhancements, and monitor whether implemented changes successfully reduce future fraud losses.
focus: Roles of Analytics, Investigations, and Risk Management.
